content.value_statement: Unvalidated Python data can cause runtime failures and inconsistent API behavior. This skill guides Pydantic v2 model design, validation, configuration, and serialization.
actual_capabilities: Defines Pydantic v2 models with typed fields, defaults, aliases, and numeric or string constraints.
Validates dictionaries and JSON text through model validation methods.
Configures strictness, immutability, assignment validation, extra fields, and aliases with ConfigDict.
Creates field-level and model-level validators for custom and cross-field rules.
Controls serialization through exclusions, inclusions, aliases, serializers, and JSON-compatible output.
Models nested data, enumerations, and standalone types with TypeAdapter.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and examples but does not execute or test generated models.
The examples target Pydantic v2 and may require changes for Pydantic v1 projects.
The illustrated email validator checks only for a marker and is not production-grade validation.
Some enhanced types, such as EmailStr, require optional dependencies.

use_cases.title: Validate API payloads
use_cases.description: Define request and response models with constraints, aliases, nested objects, and controlled serialization.

use_cases.title: Normalize pipeline records
use_cases.description: Validate dictionaries, coerce compatible values, and report structured errors before downstream processing.

use_cases.title: Modernize validation models
use_cases.description: Apply Pydantic v2 configuration, validators, serializers, and TypeAdapter patterns to an existing Python library.

prompt_templates.title: Define a basic model
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Pydantic v2 model for [entity] with these fields: [fields]. Include sensible defaults, constraints, and one valid input example.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a new typed data model.

prompt_templates.title: Add validation rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this Pydantic v2 model for [requirements]. Add field constraints, custom validators, clear errors, and handling for extra fields.

prompt_templates.title: Control serialized output
prompt_templates.prompt: Design serialization for [model]. Exclude sensitive fields, apply aliases, format [special values], and explain the selected model_dump options.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare safe API or storage output.

prompt_templates.title: Architect a validation layer
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Pydantic v2 validation layer for [workflow]. Use nested models, strict configuration, reusable validators, TypeAdapter, and explicit serialization rules.

output_examples.input: Create a customer signup model with a positive identifier, validated email, optional signup date, and active status.
output: A Customer model uses constrained fields and a validated email type.
The signup date accepts a compatible date-time value or remains empty.
Invalid identifiers and email addresses produce clear validation errors.

output_examples.input: Protect credentials when serializing a user model.
output_examples.output: The design stores the password as a secret value, excludes it from exported data, and documents the chosen serialization options.

output_examples.input: Validate a list of integer identifiers without creating a full model.
output_examples.output: A TypeAdapter validates the list, converts compatible string values, and reports invalid elements with their locations.

best_practices: Use specific field types and constraints so invalid data fails at the model boundary.
Choose ConfigDict behavior explicitly for coercion, extra fields, assignment, and aliases.
Test valid inputs, invalid inputs, error locations, and serialized output for every important model.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on broad primitive types when the domain has stricter limits.
Do not expose secret or internal fields through default serialization.
Do not place unrelated side effects inside validators or serializers.

faq.question: Does this skill support Pydantic v1?
faq.answer: No. Its APIs and examples target Pydantic v2, so v1 projects require migration changes.

faq.question: Can it validate dictionaries and JSON text?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers model_validate for Python data and model_validate_json for JSON text.

faq.question: Can it create custom validation logic?
faq.answer: Yes. It demonstrates field validators and model validators for field-specific and cross-field rules.

faq.question: How does it help protect sensitive fields?
faq.answer: It covers SecretStr, excluded fields, selective exports, and explicit serialization options.

faq.question: Does it support nested models and enumerations?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes nested model relationships and string or integer enumeration fields.

faq.question: Does it install Pydantic automatically?
faq.answer: No. It lists uv installation commands, but users or agents must run them separately.
